repo.description:
## Summary

SurrealDB's JWKS preflight and redirect policy use `Url::port()`. That method returns `None` when an HTTP or HTTPS URL uses its implicit default port. The checked `NetTarget` therefore loses the effective port, and a rule such as `deny-net 127.0.0.1:80` or `deny-net internal.example:443` does not match. A database Owner can make SurrealDB send a JWKS GET to the explicitly denied service.

The issue is present in v3.2.0 and current main. It is a JWKS-path sibling of the earlier port-specific redirect policy issue, and remains after the v3.2.0 JWKS DNS and redirect hardening.

## Impact

A database Owner can configure a JWT or record access method with a JWKS URL targeting an implicitly addressed default port that the process operator explicitly denied. SurrealDB sends a server-side GET across that network policy boundary. The response remains blind and is parsed only as JWKS, but the primitive permits denied internal host/service reachability, timing or JWKS-parse-success inference, and interaction with internal GET endpoints on port 80 or 443.

## Reproduction

A focused test binds a valid JWKS canary to loopback port 80, constructs a datastore with all network targets allowed except `127.0.0.1:80`, and calls the real JWKS `config()` path with `http://127.0.0.1/jwks.json`. It runs in a Linux user/network namespace so the test process can bind port 80 without host privileges.

```bash
unshare -Urn sh -c 'ip link set lo up; cargo test -p surrealdb-core --lib --features jwks iam::jwks::tests::test_deny_specific_implicit_default_port_e2e_canary -- --nocapture'
```

The unmodified v3.2.0 behavior produces:

```text
deny-net=127.0.0.1:80 implicit_url result_ok=true canary_hit=true
BUG: denied loopback:80 JWKS endpoint was fetched
```

A positive control with `deny-net 127.0.0.1:8080` and an explicit `:8080` URL is rejected because the non-default port remains present.

## Root cause

`check_capabilities_url()` in `surrealdb/core/src/iam/jwks.rs` builds `host[:port]` with `url_parsed.port()`. The redirect policy repeats the same operation with `attempt.url().port()`. For default ports these return `None`, so capability matching receives only the host. `NetTarget::Host(host, Some(port))` deny rules require a target carrying the same port and therefore do not match.

The shared DNS resolver cannot restore the decision because reqwest gives it only a DNS name, then it checks host-only and IP-only targets. The general protected HTTP client already avoids this issue by using `url.port_or_known_default()`.

## Remediation

Use `port_or_known_default()` in both the initial JWKS URL check and the JWKS redirect policy. Add direct and redirect regression tests for implicit HTTP port 80 and HTTPS port 443 under matching port-specific deny rules. The two-line change made the same end-to-end canary produce `result_ok=false canary_hit=false`.
repo.summary: JWKS fetch bypasses port-specific deny-net rules on implicit default ports
